claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy can be prepared as a fully homogenized, single-phase solid solution.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is an appropriate baseline solid-solution alloy.
The dynamic behavior of Co-free FeNiCrMn undergoes a temperature- and strain-rate-dependent transition in deformation mechanism.
Removing Co reduces solute pinning in FeNiCrMn relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Removing Co alters the stacking-fault energy of the alloy.
Changes in solute pinning and stacking-fault energy alter the balance between dislocation slip and deformation twinning.
The absence of Co changes lattice distortion, dislocation configurations, and deformation-twin density.
Lower temperatures and/or higher strain rates promote deformation twinning in the Co-free alloy.
Deformation twins impede dislocation motion and increase strain hardening.
Elevated temperatures and/or lower strain rates enhance thermally activated dislocation glide.
Enhanced thermally activated glide produces a smoother, less serrated stress-strain response.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will exhibit more twins and a higher strain-hardening rate under low-temperature/high-rate conditions.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will exhibit diminished flow serrations under high-temperature/low-rate conditions.
The proposed deformation-mode shift will maintain a balanced strength-ductility profile in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi exhibits prominent solute pinning and mixed dislocation-twinning deformation under comparable conditions.
A temperature range below approximately 900 K can preserve a single-phase Co-free FeNiCrMn microstructure.
The hypothesis does not apply once phase transformations or substantial precipitation occur.
